anya: FYI seeing p95 climb on /chat-route after the microbatcher tweak, ~120ms -> ~320ms for a subset of requests. Rolling traces attached.
kevin: ugh. is this the kernel switchover canary? Which commit? :grimacing:
maria: yes it lines up with kernel-selector v2.4.1 canary. I suspect the batch formation changed token allocation per request.
anya: exact commit is `svc/runtime@d4fc2a`. Deploy logs:
deploy-bot: deploy svc/runtime d4fc2a -> v2.4.1 to canary (hosts: gtx-canary-1..3)
kevin: quick profiler dump from canary node (short):
```
2026-03-17T14:02:11Z p95=322ms p50=45ms batch_size_avg=7 token_budget=24 kv_hit=0.72
2026-03-17T14:02:13Z p95=310ms p50=46ms batch_size_avg=6 token_budget=16 kv_hit=0.71
```
kevin: token_budget oscillating down when queue policy enforces strict fairness across routes. That hurts long-context requests.
maria: for SLO-driven batching we wanted dynamic token targets per route/tier — route-level p95 target -> budget floor/ceiling. Did we accidentally fallback to global min?
anya: looks like it. The new selector computes kernel score then normalizes token shares globally before per-route clamping.
ryan: proposal: implement a per-route SLO multiplier that biases token slices if route p95 > target. Simple version: `route_budget = base_budget * min(1.0, slo_target / observed_p95)`
kevin: careful: dividing p95 values is noisy. Use smoothed p95 over a minute window and cap multiplier to [0.5, 2.0]. Also tie to kv_hit ratio: if kv_hit<0.6 then prefer larger budgets.
maria: agreed. Also we should avoid microbatch starvation: add `min_tokens_reserved=8` for premium routes.
anya: sketch of config (WIP):
```
batching:
  base_budget: 24
  per_route_overrides:
    /chat-route:
      slo_target_ms: 150
      min_tokens_reserved: 8
      max_mult: 2.0
  smoothing_window_s: 60
  kv_hit_threshold: 0.6
```
anya: if we push this into canary, we can watch p95 delta and batch_size distributions.
ryan: also add a kernel sampling flag so the selector can prefer kernels that reduce tail (we saw prefetched-kernel increased tail for long sequences).
kevin: I'm going to run an offline sim comparing current vs proposed policy on last 6h trace. Will post numbers.
maria: thanks. If sim looks good, roll to canary and set canary throttle to 5% and watch p95, kv_hit, and batch_size_pctiles. :eyes:
andeploy: ack — I'll add a tmp metric `slo_budget.multiplier` to dashboards and alert if multiplier > 1.5 for >2m on a route.
deploy-bot: scheduled: canary update with `slo-batch-multiplier` flag (5% traffic) at 2026-03-18T09:00:00Z
kevin: sim results (quick):
```
baseline: p95=315ms, p99=780ms, avg_batch=6.8
proposal: p95=165ms, p99=420ms, avg_batch=5.9
notes: token spend +6%, kv_hit stable
```
kevin: seems promising. Will open a short PR with the config & sampling flag.
anya: awesome. please include the trace links and flamegraphs. Also add a note to the rollout playbook: `if p95 increases >10% after flag, revert`.
maria: I'll monitor dashboards and be on watch during rollout window. :rocket:
ryan: nice work, team. keep the runtimes happy. :thumbsup:
